decisions.statement: An audit is refused for the memory a run has rather than for the changes a run writes.
A subagent is told from its seat by the subagent id the payload names.
A call the seat itself makes is not refused.
A prefix that only runs the call behind that prefix does not hide that call from this hook.
The refusal says a run's cost.
A run narrowed to named checks is refused.
A run narrowed to named paths is refused.
A run naming no check and no path asks the service, so that run is refused here by nothing.
A narrowed run asks the service like a bare run, so the cost this refusal names is gone.
A run's cost is said as a figure measured rather than as a figure supposed.
Every akasha command but `audit` is no business of this hook.
A payload naming no subagent leaves the call as the call is.
A payload this cannot read judges nothing and exits so the dispatch refuses.
A payload that parses and is not an object is a payload this cannot read.
A harness naming no subagent refuses nobody rather than refusing everyone.

definition: a refusal of an `akasha audit` a subagent narrows, the bare call left through for anyone
